findings.where: the whole plinth, x 166-1436, y 492-1509; clearest at the back edge, x 300-1250, y 440-600
findings.what: The clear plinth is an even, cold white sheet: L* 98.1-99.1, a* -1.3, b* 0 (rgb 248/252/252) everywhere that is not covered. It is brighter than the floor it stands on (floor in front 92.6, at the left 82.7; in linear light the plinth is 1.14/1.20/1.28 times the front floor in R/G/B) and it has lost the floor's warmth (floor b* +3.9 to +5.2). The smoked base is gone: over the base 98.1, over the margin 98.7 (before: 15-29 against 68-76). The black box reads L* 50-74 (before 4-13). The shadow of the record and motor cover on the floor (L* 59-66 just outside the back edge) stops dead at the edge; 20 px inside, the plinth reads 98.8, a step of +33 to +39 L*. 14.0% of the frame is now at 245 or above in all channels (before 0.2%). It reads as white laminate or a lightbox, not as clear acrylic.
findings.expected: A clear sheet can only pass on what is under it. Each face reflects 3.9%, so one pass lets 0.92 through; light down and view up gives 0.85, plus about 7% from light bouncing between floor and sheet: about 0.9 of the open floor, so L* 87-91 beside floor at 92.6, with the floor's warm tint, never brighter. The shadow must run on under the back margin (about L* 60-70, softened), and the smoked base must show as a soft dark gray rectangle. The sheet also cannot both pass the light (the floor shadow behind it did get 8 L* lighter) and send all of it back like white paper. The picture proves the true values itself: inside the two streaks (next finding) the margin reads 84-90 and the base 33-48. I do not know the cause; no shadow of the record falls on the white, so it is not key light caught by the satin face.

findings.where: streak 1: x 470-1436, y 613-753 (hidden under the record from x 540 to 910); streak 2: x 1160-1436, y 990-1070
findings.what: Two straight gray bands run exactly left to right across the white plinth, out to its right edge and past the base's footprint. Streak 1 is 140 px (50 mm) tall and starts at the motor; streak 2 is 80 px (28 mm) tall and sits at the height of the record's center (y 1033). Their top and bottom edges switch within about 10 px over a run of 300 px and more. Inside them: L* 50-74 over the black box, 33-48 over the base, rising 54 to 90 toward the right edge. The sockets are four smeared light blobs at the top of streak 1. Nothing was there before (right margin flat at L* 83).
findings.expected: Nothing straight-edged. Bead-blast blurs evenly in all directions, and the key's shadows in this frame are soft over 100-200 px and fall up and to the right (the spindle's shadow on the label points 26 degrees right of straight up), so these are not shadows of the key and not satin blur. Each band starts at a hole through the plinth (motor, bearing) and runs to one edge; inside the bands the deck looks the way it should (previous finding). That pattern points at the plinth's faces or normals around the cut-outs behaving in two different ways under the new shadow setup; that part is my guess.

findings.where: all four plinth edges; e.g. front edge x 300-700, y 1480-1530; front left corner x 160-260, y 1440-1520
findings.what: The plinth has no outline. Across the front edge L* goes 99 to 92 with no line at all; right and back edges the same; the left edge keeps a 2 px dip to 73. Before, every edge had a dark line (L* 25-62) and a bright one beside it, and the corners showed their radius. The 25 mm slab now reads as a paper cut-out. Same fault as the white plinth, most likely; listed so it gets checked after the repair.
findings.expected: From above with this lens the satin side faces show as strips a few px wide, and the 1 mm polished chamfer gives a thin line that is lighter or darker than the top. A photograph of a 25 mm clear slab always shows its edge.

findings.where: arm foot x 1170-1230, y 940-995; foot of the arm-rest post x 1095-1125, y 960-995. Same part in the top view: white ring x 1217-1275, y 670-795 of mantle-house-fog-top-test.png
findings.what: The white patch at the arm's foot is still there, the same size and tone as before: 742 px above 200 in all channels, mean rgb 244/245/248 (before 715 px, 243/247/249). It shows a rim, so it is a part with thickness, like a white washer. The foot of the rest post has the same thing: 104 px, rgb 253/241/241 (before 96 px, 249/249/250). In the new frame both also throw a pink-white hot spot onto the pillar and post, and a red glow sits under the front rim of the flange. It is the brightest thing on the red deck and draws the eye. Whatever was made satin black, this was not it.
findings.expected: Nothing white on this deck: all hardware is satin black and the plinth is red. In a ring-shaped gap at the arm's foot one would see dark red plinth or a black part. A neutral white part in every color (it is white in the red and the clear deck, before and now) looks like a piece with no material set.

findings.what: Seen from straight above, the finger lift is a loose black bar beside the headshell. A gap of 6-8 px (2-3 mm) of bare plinth (L* 95-96) runs between its end and the headshell plate over the whole width of the bar, so nothing joins them at any height. Now that the arm is parked off the record the gap sits against a light ground and shows.
findings.expected: A finger lift is part of the headshell; from above the two must touch.

findings.what: The finger lift points toward the record (the inner side of the headshell). It did before as well.
findings.expected: On the Rega arms I know the finger lift is on the outer side, away from the record, so the right hand can take it. From memory, not from a drawing: check against the RB330.

findings.what: Where the plinth is lit (roughly its left third) it is the speaker's red, a little lighter and milkier: rgb 216/49/43, L* 48.2, C* 76.7, hue 35.0 against the speaker's horn at 207/12/8, L* 43.7, C* 86.9, hue 39.2 (difference about 12.6 dE). The rest of the top is maroon-brown, L* 18-21, C* 16-17 (rgb 64/36/31 and 72/42/36), where the speaker's shaded red stays pure (78/0/0, L* 13.3, C* 39.1). New is a shade redder than before in both zones (C* 76.7 against 71.9; 15.7 against 11.7). So: same red, not as deep over most of the top.
findings.expected: This is not a renderer fault. At this low camera (about 18 degrees) the view goes through the plinth into the gap and onto the dark smoked base, so little red comes back, and the glossy top adds a thin gray sheen (green and blue near 40 where the speaker has 0-10). A real deck would do the same. If the owner wants the deck to read red all over in this view, that is a choice about the base or the camera height, not about this render.

findings.where: plinth top right of the platter, x 780-1280, y 1040-1260
findings.what: The grain is down by about two thirds, not half: fine-grain spread on the floor 1.05 against 2.95 before, on the plinth top 0.8-0.9 against 1.9-2.2. At normal size the frame is cleaner. On the dark plinth top the smoothing now shows as soft clouds and streaks when the crop is brightened three times; at normal exposure it passes. No banding in the sweep.
findings.expected: Fine as it is. I would not take the grain any lower: it is what keeps the dark, smoothed surfaces from looking airbrushed.

findings.what: Two small lens-shaped marks sit just under the top edge of the plinth's long front face, each about 22 mm wide. They were there before. At full size they read as dents or smudges in the edge. They may be the bumpers seen through the plinth; I cannot tell.
findings.expected: A satin face would blur a bumper behind it to nothing; a crisp lens shape there looks like a flaw. A retoucher would take them out of a photograph.

findings.where: x 672-705, y 1184-1204, in the gap under the plinth
findings.what: The bumper in the gap is a neutral, slightly cool gray dome: rgb 132/131/134, L* 54.8, a* +0.9, b* -1.4. Everything around it in the gap is lit red. Same before.
findings.expected: A white or clear bumper under a red plinth, over a red-lit base and a warm floor, would pick up some red or warmth. A dead neutral gray looks pasted in. Small in the frame.

findings.where: record, x 400-1080, y 800-1000; the same in the top view
findings.what: The record is a smooth satin disc with five or six thin scribed rings. In the three-quarter frame its far half goes to a mid gray with no structure. Unchanged from before. The blank label is good: plain warm paper, two thin rings, a soft spindle shadow.
findings.expected: Vinyl under a soft key shows a fan of sheen that follows the grooves, with bands of slightly different sheen per track. Its absence is a mild tell at full size, not at page size.

found.q1_red_ready: Not yet, though it is close. As a photograph the red frame holds and is better than before: the arm is parked with the cartridge clear, the label is blank, the grain is cleaner, the floor now picks up a faint red from the deck as a real floor would, and the ground is unchanged (all seven ground patches within 0.1 L* of before). Two things stop it: the white patch at the arm's foot and at the rest post's foot is still in the frame exactly as before, and the shadow change this pattern carries breaks the clear deck from above, which the red test cannot show. Fix the white parts, repair the clear deck, then test a clear deck in three-quarter view and one tinted deck from above before the set is rendered; neither was tested here.
found.q2_clear_from_above_true: No. Such a deck from above would show the floor through the 35 mm margin at about nine tenths of the open floor's brightness (L* 87-91 beside 92.6) and with its warm tint, the record's shadow running on under the back margin, the smoked base as a soft-edged dark gray rectangle with the box, motor and posts as darker soft shapes, and a thin line all around where the chamfer and satin edge show. The picture shows an even cold white sheet at L* 98.1-99.1, brighter than the floor, with no base, a shadow that stops at the back edge, no outline, and two straight gray streaks; only inside those streaks does it look right (margin 84-90, base 33-48). The picture before was closer to true, apart from being too dark under the margins.
found.q3_reads_as_cg: In the top view: the white, self-lit plinth, the two hard-edged streaks, the missing edge line, and the finger lift floating beside the headshell. In the red frame: the white patch and pink hot spot at the arm's foot and rest post, then, at full size only, the record without groove sheen, the neutral gray bumper in a red-lit gap, the two lens marks on the front face, and the very smooth dark plinth top now that the grain is lower.

findings.what: The clear plinth is a flat near-white slab: sRGB about 248/252/252, L* 98.3 to 99.0, the same within 2 levels over the floor margin on all four sides and over the smoked base. It is lighter than every patch of floor in the frame (floor L* 84.4 left, 88.7 right, 91.7 front, 93 in the corners; the paper label is L* 65.6). In luminance (sRGB decoded) it is 1.49 (left), 1.22 (front), 1.30 (right) and 2.74 (back, where the floor behind is in the deck's shadow) times the floor beside it. Its cast is cool (b* -0.1 to -1.0); the floor is warm (b* +3.7 to +5.7), so this light has not come off the floor. The smoked base, a dark soft rectangle before (L* 36 to 37), is gone: the step at its edge is 2 levels of red. The black box (L* 8 to 10 before) is L* 55 in its back part and L* 71 to 84 in its front part. No edge or chamfer line is left at the outline, and the record and arm throw no shadow onto or under the slab. Cause not found from the picture: a toy test of the obvious suspect (lamp light joined straight through the top face onto the frosted face, veil_toy.py) gives only 0.06 to 0.15 of a white card.
findings.expected: A clear slab with a glossy top and a frosted underside sends up three things: what the floor below returns, cut about 4 percent at the top face and 5 to 10 percent at the frosted face; a few percent of haze scattered back by the frost; and a 4 percent mirror of whatever is overhead. My Monte Carlo of that stack (n 1.49, roughness 0.3 to 0.5, floor albedo 0.7 to 0.9, key 40 to 60 degrees off vertical; slab_mc.py) gives, relative to the open floor: margin 0.87 to 0.99, over the smoked base 0.07 to 0.21, over black 0.07 to 0.16. So a true picture shows the margin slightly darker than the floor beside it (about L* 87 to 91 where the floor is 91.7, darker at the back where the floor under it lies in the record's shadow), the base as a dark soft-edged rectangle near L* 28 to 48, the box as a blurred block near L* 28 to 43, never black and never white. A passive clear slab cannot return more light than the white floor under it; to read L* 98.8 it would have to reflect 1.2 to 1.5 times what the floor reflects. If the view transform has a shoulder the real excess is larger, not smaller. The before frame is nearer the truth at all three places: margin 0.69 to 0.88 of the adjacent floor (too dark by 0.1 to 0.2), base 0.13 to 0.14 (inside my range), box 0.01 to 0.02 (too black by 20 to 30 L*, but still a box).

findings.where: Three horizontal bands right of the record: x 960-1430, y 600-750; x 1160-1430, y 990-1070; x 1100-1430, y 1252-1340.
findings.what: Gray smears run from the record's rim to the plinth's right edge. Middle band: sRGB about 80 to 85 at x 1180-1200, 135 at x 1300, 220 at x 1380 (the white around it is 249); it sits at the height of the spindle (y 1034) and is about 70 px (25 mm) thick. Upper band (L* 47 to 59) sits at the height of the motor (y 674) and holds what is left of the black box and its sockets. Lower band is faint (243 to 247 against 249), about 88 px (31 mm) thick. In the before frame the same area is an even gray gradient (sRGB 48 to 110) with no bars. Left of the record there are no bands (left margin stays 248 from y 780 to 1500).
findings.expected: Nothing in the design makes a horizontal bar there. The key at about 40 degrees throws a shadow about 1.2 times the caster's height, under 50 mm for anything in the 40 mm gap, not a trail of 100 mm and more. A true picture shows this area as the smoked base, an even dark gray through the frost. The bands say the light that whitens the slab travels sideways, left to right, inside the slab or in the gap under it, and is cut off by things on its way (spindle bearing, motor, perhaps the posts). Probably the same fault as optics-1; listed apart because it shows where the extra light goes and must be gone in the re-test.

findings.where: Plinth top, right half, x 820-1330, y 960-1230.
findings.what: The top face does not read glossy; it reads satin. On the deep red plinth the green channel holds only what the top face reflects (the red body passes no green: G is 1 to 3 where the top mirrors black parts). That reflection is a soft cloud: along x 1050 green rises from 1 at y 1000 to 50 at y 1120 with no edge anywhere. The arm tube's mirror image is a broad dim band and the lift post's reflection is a smear that widens with distance. Same in the before frame, so this is not from today's change.
findings.expected: A cast, glossy acrylic face seen about 66 degrees from its normal (camera about 24 degrees above the surface, from the record's ellipse 270 by 676 px) mirrors about 13 percent (Fresnel, n 1.49). It would show crisp, dark mirror images of the arm tube (roughly 150 to 200 px below the tube), counterweight, lift post and platter rim against the reflected wall, with edges as sharp as the parts themselves. The blur seen is about 5 to 10 degrees, which is a satin finish.

findings.where: Arm pillar foot x 1180-1250, y 945-985; lift post foot x 1095-1130, y 960-1000.
findings.what: New in this frame: red-hot flares on the black pillar and on the lift post just above their feet (31 px and 9 px with red at 250 or more and green under 150; none in the before frame). The white disc at the pillar's foot and the white dot at the post's foot are still at 255 (576 px at 240 or more in all channels; 548 before). In the top view the same disc shows as a white ring inside the black arm base.
findings.expected: Satin black hardware beside a red slab can pick up a dull red sheen low on its lit side, but not a clipped red patch: its reflectance is a few percent except at grazing angles. A part at 255 next to a floor at 239 is as bright as a perfect white card or a mirror of a lamp. With all hardware satin black nothing there should be white or glowing.

findings.where: Strip along the plinth's left edge on the top face (the 35 mm margin seen at a shallow angle), about x 150-620, y 780-1060.
findings.what: 8,177 px in that strip have more red than the open white floor (linear red above 0.863); their mean is sRGB 247/91/90, linear red 0.935. Before: 7,743 px. Taking off the white sheen (the green level, 0.117) leaves 0.82 of red that came through the slab, which is 0.95 of the floor's red. Only 54 px clip at 255.
findings.expected: Through that strip the camera sees, via the frost, the open lit floor beyond the deck's left side. The most a red slab can pass is 0.86 (top face at this angle) times about 0.93 (frost) times the acrylic's own red transmission over a 32 mm slant path. With no absorption at all that is 0.80 of the floor's red, plus a few percent of haze; a deep red would give 0.5 to 0.7. So the strip is 10 to 20 percent brighter in red than a loss-free filter allows and reads as lit from inside. I cannot rule out that the view transform bends bright saturated reds, so this stays a note.

findings.where: Floor around the deck: left x 0-300, y 1085-1170; front x 780-860, y 1320-1390; right x 1255-1335, y 1140-1180.
findings.what: Yes, there is now red on the floor beside the red deck, and none before. Red channel up by 0.02 to 0.10 (linear; open floor 0.86), green and blue unchanged to within 0.005. a* goes from about -0.5 to +1 to +3 at the sides and peaks at +6.8 in front of the base (x 800-840, y 1340-1360). L* rises by 2 at most. The red that comes back is 10 to 26 percent of the light the deck takes away at each place.
findings.expected: Right in kind: a red slab passes red only, so its shadow stays almost as dark and turns pink. In amount it looks low. The slab should pass roughly 0.8 of red per pass, and about half of the rays through the plinth then meet the record or the black parts, so I would expect 30 to 45 percent back, a pink about twice as strong. The floor alone cannot settle which tint the shadow rays use; ask the lane for the number and compare it with the red the camera sees through the plinth (which behaves like 0.8 or more per pass).
